key_insight: SAGE-Net injects crystallographic semantics directly into geometric message passing, letting text-derived structure descriptors actively guide atom-level crystal graph learning for better property prediction.
engineering_relevance: This makes multimodal materials models more transferable and physically informed, improving predictions for screening candidate materials in design and discovery workflows.
method: Semantic-Guided Message Passing (SGMP) gates atom updates using description-derived chemical and crystallographic semantics.
The framework can be attached to multiple GNN backbones for flexible multimodal learning.
It combines structural graphs with crystallographic descriptions instead of fusing text only after encoding.
evidence_signal: Across JARVIS-DFT benchmarks, SAGE-Net achieved the lowest MAE on 8 of 10 regression targets and showed strong synthesizability classification performance with high recall.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and consistency of the crystallographic descriptions used to generate semantic signals, which could limit robustness across datasets.
paper_title: SAGE-Net: Semantics-Augmented Geometric Encoder for Material Property Prediction
